title.narrative: IDF Grant for Creating Institutional Capacity for Reforming Sri Lanka's Pension Reform

description.narrative: The purpose of this grant would be to assist the GOSL to achieve optimal outcomes in pension reform by helping build institutional capacity in designing and implementing the planned pension schemes. The grant would be used to develop capacity within the GoSL to (a) produce and interpret actuarial projections of pension finances for the public sector pension schemes and assess the fiscal implications of reforms; (b) formulate different design options; (c) propose sound governance mechanisms for publicly sponsored programs; (d) prepare a cash-flow model to support new investment policies of the amalgamated EPF/ETF and development of these policies; and (e) analyze the tax treatment and other related areas of public policy that would have a bearing on the design of the pension system. These objectives would be met through targeted training programscomma workshopscomma study tours and technical reports on specific issues by international and local consultants. The activities can be usefully grouped into two separate components. Component 1 will focus on public sector pensions and Component 2 will deal with pension schemes for private sector employees. Component 1 would assist the Government in further shaping the design of the Contributory Pension Fund and in stabilizing expenditures of the Public Sector Pension Scheme. The Government will be faced with a number of policy issues that concern the CPFcomma including (i) actuarial assessment of different options for the scheme.s design; (ii) investment policy; (iii) governance mechanisms and regulatory framework; (iv) collection of contributions and recordkeeping infrastructure; and (v) member education. With respect to the PSPScomma the component will assist the GOSL in evaluating options to stabilize the scheme.s future expenditures and improving benefit design so that retirement income is not front-loaded leaving members with low-value pensions during their advanced retirement years. Component 2 would assist the Government in the development of a sounder policy framework for retirement savings schemes for private sector workerscomma especially with the establishment of (i) a sound governance structure for the EPF or the amalgamated EPF/ETFcomma if the government proceeds with the amalgamation; (ii) definition of options to move from a retirement savings plan with a monolithic investment portfolio to a plan with greater portfolio choice and greater fund management by the private sector; (iii) the regulatory framework of these provident funds; and (iv) member education. Strengthen institutional capacity to design and implement the pension reform.
